answer: select avg(n) from (select b.molecule_id, count(*) n from bond b join molecule m using(molecule_id) where m.label='+' and b.bond_type='-' group by 1)

select count(distinct case when a.element='i' then a.atom_id end) as iodine, count(distinct case when a.element='s' then a.atom_id end) as sulfur from atom a join connected c on c.atom_id=a.atom_id join bond b on b.bond_id=c.bond_id where b.bond_type='-'
select count(*) from atom where molecule_id in (select molecule_id from bond where bond_type='#') and molecule_id in (select molecule_id from atom where element in ('p','br'))

select a.molecule_id, count(distinct c.bond_id) as bond_count from atom a join molecule m on m.molecule_id=a.molecule_id and m.label='+' join connected c on c.atom_id=a.atom_id where a.element in (select element from atom group by element having count(distinct molecule_id)=1) group by a.molecule_id order by a.molecule_id
select round(1.0*(select count(*) from connected c join atom a on a.atom_id=c.atom_id where a.molecule_id='TR397')/(select count(*) from atom where molecule_id='TR397'),2) as avg_bonds

select a.element, count(*) as atom_count from atom a where exists(select 1 from connected c join bond b using(bond_id) where c.atom_id=a.atom_id and b.bond_type='-') and not exists(select 1 from connected c join bond b using(bond_id) where c.atom_id=a.atom_id and b.bond_type in ('=','#')) group by a.element order by a.element
